title: Member of Technical Staff (Enterprise Security Engineer)
description_html:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Perplexity is growing fast, and every new employee, laptop, SaaS app and integration expands what we have to protect. We want enterprise security that's strong by default, mostly automated, and invisible to people doing their jobs.



We're looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer to own the security of how Perplexity works internally: our identities, devices, SaaS applications and corporate access. You'll sit on the Security Engineering team and work closely with IT, building controls and automation together so the secure path is also the easy one.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own identity security: SSO and MFA policy, conditional access and device trust, privileged and admin access, service accounts, and break-glass procedures.

 - Harden our SaaS stack. Manage OAuth app and integration risk, admin roles, sharing and retention settings, and audit logging across our core collaboration and productivity tools.

 - Define and enforce endpoint security baselines with IT, across EDR, device management, disk encryption, OS and browser policy, and software allowlisting.

 - Build access governance that scales: just-in-time and request-based access, regular access reviews, and joiner/mover/leaver automation that removes access promptly and reliably.

 - Write detections for corporate threats such as account takeover, OAuth abuse, data exfiltration, insider risk and malicious extensions, and respond when they fire.

 - Automate everything you can. Write code and infrastructure-as-code to configure systems, remediate drift, and replace manual tickets with self-service workflows.

 - Secure corporate network access and email, including zero-trust remote access, phishing protection and domain security.

 - Partner with IT, People, Legal and GRC on new tools and vendors, security reviews, and evidence for compliance programs.



QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years in security engineering, with significant time on corporate or enterprise security, identity, or endpoint security.

 - Hands-on depth with at least one major identity provider (such as Okta or Entra ID), including SSO, SCIM, MFA and conditional access policy.

 - Experience securing SaaS environments such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, Slack, and developer tools, including OAuth and third-party app risk.

 - Experience with endpoint security and device management across macOS (and ideally Windows and Linux), including EDR, MDM and configuration baselines.

 - Proficiency in at least one programming language (such as Python or Go) and comfort building automation against vendor APIs. Experience with infrastructure-as-code is a plus.

 - Experience writing detections and investigating incidents with a SIEM or log platform.

 - Good judgment about trade-offs between security and productivity, and the ability to roll out controls without slowing the company down.

 - Bonus: experience at a fast-growing company where you built enterprise security from an early stage.

 - Bonus: experience securing AI tools and agents in the workplace, such as agent access to SaaS data, browser agents, and AI app governance.
$250K – $350K

title: Member of Technical Staff (Cybersecurity Solutions Architect)
description_html:
Enterprises are rolling Perplexity out to thousands of employees and connecting it to their most sensitive internal data. Their security teams want to know how to do that safely, and they want to hear it from someone who has done real security work.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Cybersecurity Solutions Architect to be that person. You'll be the security expert our enterprise customers work with as they deploy Perplexity: running architecture and hardening sessions with their security leads, reviewing how they're configuring identity, data access, and admin controls, and helping them get to a setup they're confident in. You'll sit on the Security team and work closely with our enterprise sales, customer success, and product teams, and you'll bring what you learn from customers back into how we build and secure the product.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead security architecture workshops and hardening reviews with enterprise customers' security and IT teams as they deploy Perplexity. This covers identity and SSO/SCIM, connectors to internal data, access controls, data retention, admin and audit settings, and managed browser and endpoint policy.

 - Act as the technical security voice in strategic enterprise deals. Answer deep security reviews and questionnaires, and represent our security posture to CISOs and security architects.

 - Build and maintain the materials customers rely on: hardening guides, reference architectures, configuration baselines, and security FAQs.

 - Help customers configure enterprise controls in their own environments, such as identity providers, MDM and device management tools like Microsoft Intune, and data source permissions. Troubleshoot when something doesn't apply as expected.

 - Turn recurring customer security requests into product feedback. Work with product and engineering to prioritize the controls enterprises need.

 - Partner with account executives and customer success on customer-specific security asks, and know when to bring in Security Engineering or Legal.

 - Track common customer concerns and gaps, and help shape how we communicate security and trust externally.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years in security engineering, security architecture, or a customer-facing security role such as solutions architect, sales engineer, or security consultant.

 - Hands-on depth in enterprise identity and access (SSO, SAML/OIDC, SCIM, conditional access) and in SaaS security configuration.

 - Working knowledge of the Microsoft ecosystem (Entra ID, Intune, M365, Purview) and at least one other major enterprise stack, such as Google Workspace or Okta.

 - Comfortable leading technical conversations with CISOs and security architects. Able to say no, explain trade-offs plainly, and earn trust in the room.

 - Familiarity with compliance frameworks enterprise customers ask about, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and FedRAMP, and with how they map to product controls.

 - Clear written communication. You can turn a messy customer environment into a crisp set of recommendations.

 - Bonus: experience securing AI or LLM products, agent integrations, or data connectors in enterprise environments.

 - Bonus: background in browser security, endpoint management, or data loss prevention.
$250K – $350K • Offers Equity

title: Staff Enterprise Security Engineer
description_html:
ROLE SUMMARY

Join our Security team as a Staff Enterprise Security Engineer, where you'll own the security of the systems our employees rely on every day: their laptops, the SaaS applications that hold our data, and the AI assistants and agents now woven into how we work. In this position, you'll set technical direction across endpoint, SaaS, and enterprise AI security, building secure-by-default controls as code and partnering closely with IT, Detection & Response, GRC, and Engineering. You'll also build AI-assisted security workflows of your own, with the right guardrails. We're looking for someone who treats security as an engineering discipline and helps the whole company move fast, safely, as a trusted partner rather than a gatekeeper.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own endpoint security architecture for a macOS-first fleet (plus Windows, Linux, and mobile), including hardening baselines, working with IT on MDM, EDR, patching policy, application control, and device trust.

 - Manage endpoint and SaaS security configuration as code, using Terraform, version control, code review, and automated rollouts so every control is repeatable and auditable.

 - Build and run the SaaS security program: application inventory, secure configuration standards for critical platforms (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Salesforce), and drift detection.

 - Govern third-party integrations, OAuth grants, browser extensions, and non-human identities to prevent data leakage and over-privileged access.

 - Lead discovery and inventory of AI usage across the company, covering approved assistants, coding agents, MCP servers, plugins, and shadow AI.

 - Design and deploy guardrails for enterprise AI, including data loss prevention, agent and MCP access scoping, tool-call policies, and defenses against prompt injection.

 - Lead cross-functional security initiatives from proposal through rollout, partnering with IT, Engineering, Legal, and People teams: scoping the work, setting milestones, managing stakeholders, and reporting progress and outcomes to leadership.

 - Perform threat modeling and security reviews of new SaaS vendors, AI tools, agents, and internal integrations.

 - Stay current on emerging standards and guidance (e.g. OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF, MCP security specifications) and translate these into actionable internal policy.

 - Partner with Detection & Response to ensure endpoints, identity, SaaS, and AI platforms produce the telemetry needed for detection, and automate response workflows.

 - Mentor engineers across Security and IT, and serve as the senior escalation point for complex enterprise security issues.

 - Able to participate in on-call rotation.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

 - 7+ years in enterprise security, corporate security, or a related role, including technical leadership of initiatives that span multiple teams.

 - Deep hands-on experience securing endpoint fleets at scale, with MDM (e.g. Jamf, Kandji, Fleet, Intune) and EDR (e.g. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) platforms and macOS hardening.

 - Proven ability to model SaaS threats, assess vendor and integration risk, and harden configurations across platforms such as Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, and Salesforce.

 - Strong knowledge of identity as the foundation of SaaS and device security: SSO, federation, SCIM provisioning, conditional access, and device posture enforcement.

 - Practical understanding of AI security risks, including prompt injection, data leakage, insecure tool connectors, and over-privileged agents, and experience putting guardrails around AI assistants and coding agents.

 - Ability to write production-quality code in at least one language (e.g. Python or Go), with a history of building automation and security tooling beyond simple scripting.

 - Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code and GitOps workflows (Terraform, CI/CD pipelines) and with SOAR or workflow automation platforms.

 - A track record of leading projects that span several teams outside Security, from getting them prioritized through delivery, including clear plans, measurable success criteria, and a handoff to long-term owners.

 - Ability to influence without authority, bringing along teams whose goals and constraints differ from Security’s.

 - Excellent communication and ability to explain complex security concepts to non-technical stakeholders.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience administering enterprise AI platforms (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, Copilot) and their admin, audit, and compliance controls.

 - Building MCP servers, agents, or other AI tooling for security workflows.

 - Familiarity with SSPM, enterprise browser security, and DLP or CASB tooling.

 - Supporting audits and compliance programs such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP.

 - Experience in a remote-first company of similar size and growth stage.

 - Open Source contributions or automation projects.

 - Security conference talks or published research.

Senior DevOps / Platform Engineer - GCP
description_html:
Headquarters: Cyprus
URL: http://gomining.com

Description

We are looking for a Senior DevOps / Platform Engineer to develop and operate GoMining's cloud platform.

The primary focus of this role is GCP and Kubernetes, infrastructure and application delivery automation, and the reliability and security of production services.

You will maintain and improve our existing infrastructure, contribute to the development of the next generation of our platform, and help product teams ship changes safely and efficiently.


Responsibilities

  • Develop and operate infrastructure in GCP, including GKE, virtual machines, networking, load balancers, storage, and managed services.
  • Manage Infrastructure as Code with Terraform: develop modules, manage state and dependencies, ensure reproducible changes, and identify configuration drift.
  • Operate Kubernetes: upgrade clusters and platform components, configure autoscaling, workload placement, network policies, and resource allocation.
  • Develop CI/CD and GitOps using GitLab CI and Flux / Argo CD, automating builds, checks, deployments, controlled releases, and rollbacks.
  • Build observability across metrics, logs, distributed tracing, and actionable alerting. Define and improve SLIs/SLOstogether with engineering teams.
  • Troubleshoot production incidents and performance issues, conduct root cause analysis, and eliminate recurring failure patterns.
  • Implement least-privilege access, environment and service isolation, secure secrets management and rotation, and infrastructure audit controls.
  • Maintain backup processes and regularly validate recovery of critical data and infrastructure according to agreed RPO/RTO.
  • Help engineering teams prepare services for production, including health checks, resource configuration, telemetry, and deployment procedures.
  • Optimize cloud infrastructure usage and costs while maintaining reliability requirements.
  • Maintain infrastructure documentation, operational runbooks, and recovery procedures.


Requirements
  • Strong hands-on experience independently operating production infrastructure and Kubernetes, including upgrades, troubleshooting, and disaster recovery.
  • Strong experience with GCP, including GKE, Compute Engine, VPC, IAM, and Cloud Storage; good understanding of Cloud SQL, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Monitoring.
  • Hands-on experience with Terraform, including modules, remote state, locking, importing existing resources, and safely applying infrastructure changes through CI.
  • Deep knowledge of Kubernetes and containerization: Deployments, StatefulSets, Services, Ingress, storage, requests/limits, probes, autoscaling, RBAC, and NetworkPolicy.
  • Experience with Helm and Kustomize.
  • Strong Linux administration skills, preferably Debian/Ubuntu: processes, systemd, filesystems, disks, and resource troubleshooting.
  • Strong networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP(S), TLS, routing, NAT, load balancing, and firewalls.
  • Ability to troubleshoot connectivity issues across applications, Kubernetes clusters, networks, and cloud services.
  • Experience building CI/CD pipelines, preferably with GitLab CI, and strong understanding of Git and GitOps principles.
  • Understanding of runner permissions, secrets protection, and production deployment controls.
  • Automation skills with Bash and Python, including maintainable infrastructure scripts and API integrations.
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Cloud Monitoring.
  • Practical experience operating PostgreSQL and understanding Redis and RabbitMQ, including availability, connections, replication or clustering, backup, and recovery.
  • Strong understanding of cloud security principles: least privilege, service accounts, Workload Identity, secrets management, network segmentation, and access auditing.
  • Ability to independently deliver infrastructure changes to a validated production result, explain technical trade-offs, and collaborate effectively with Engineering and Security teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Flux CD, Argo CD, Ansible, and HashiCorp Vault.
  • Experience with OpenTelemetry and distributed tracing.
  • Experience migrating infrastructure between clouds or Kubernetes clusters, including database migrations with limited downtime.
  • Experience designing disaster recovery strategies and conducting recovery exercises.
  • Cloud cost optimization and capacity planning experience.
  • Experience with DigitalOcean, Hetzner, or AWS.
  • Ability to read and troubleshoot JavaScript / TypeScript applications.
  • Experience operating financial or payment services with strict requirements around access control, auditing, reliability, and data integrity.


Benefits
  • Professional growth: support for courses, conferences, and English learning (up to 100% coverage).
  • Work-life fit: remote or hybrid format with flexible hours across international teams.
  • Paid leave: up to 20 vacation days +  8 company holidays + 5 personal days per year
  • Recognition programs: structured performance reviews and team awards.
  • Team culture: retreats in international locations (for example, company apartments in Cyprus).

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/gomining-senior-devops-platform-engineer-gcp
